Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic thromboembolic disease. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal or only mildly enlarged, making "mild pulmonary hypertension" the most appropriate descriptor among the choices compared to options suggesting severe PH with massive cardiomegaly or normal findings.
